CurveOut.title: CurveOut

CurveSeriesOut.description: One line on a chart. Several appear when a query resolves to several series.
CurveSeriesOut.title: CurveSeriesOut

EventSourceGrafanaIn.description:
The optional Grafana address. An empty URL removes the configuration.

No `auth_type` and no `username`: Grafana here is Bearer-or-anonymous, and
an internal instance configured for anonymous read is a normal deployment,
not a misconfigured one. An absent credential *is* the anonymous case.

**Plain `http` and a private address are both accepted.** Grafana is a
read-only monitoring source living on the internal network, not an outbound
target — applying the outbound address rules here would reject the ordinary
configuration (CAP-13.1a).
EventSourceGrafanaIn.title: EventSourceGrafanaIn

EventSourceThanosIn.description: The optional history address. An empty URL means "do not backfill".
EventSourceThanosIn.title: EventSourceThanosIn

EvidenceNoteOut.description:
One entry in `warnings` or `failures`.

Same shape, different meaning: a warning means the curve is there but part of
it was inferred; a failure means the curve is not there. Merging them would
pair a working chart with an alarming message about the store being down.
EvidenceNoteOut.title: EvidenceNoteOut

FeishuChannelIn.description:
Feishu custom bot: the webhook carries its own token in the last path
segment, which is why there is no separate token field.
FeishuChannelIn.title: FeishuChannelIn

GrafanaImportItemIn.description:
A ticked candidate as the browser finally submitted it.

`final_promql` is the literal the user read on screen. The server does not
re-fetch the dashboard to rebuild it: that would look more careful and be
less so, because a definition changed between preview and confirmation would
leave the stored query different from the approved one (review Q4).
GrafanaImportItemIn.title: GrafanaImportItemIn

ImportCandidateOut.description:
One panel target, with everything the reader needs to decide about it.

Both the original and the resolved query are present: approving a
substitution means being shown what changed, not just the result.
ImportCandidateOut.title: ImportCandidateOut

IncidentOccurrenceOut.description:
One ended occurrence (F26 / CAP-11).

Everything a reader needs is on the record itself: it outlives the Incident,
the source and the rule it names, so nothing here is joined at read time.
`incident_id` is a jump hint that may already point at nothing.
IncidentOccurrenceOut.title: IncidentOccurrenceOut

IncidentOccurrencePage.description:
A keyset page. The cursor is an id, and that is only safe because the
table is append-only in recovery order -- see SYSTEM_SPEC §11.
IncidentOccurrencePage.title: IncidentOccurrencePage

MetricTemplateOriginOut.description: Where an imported template came from. Absent means hand-written.
MetricTemplateOriginOut.title: MetricTemplateOriginOut

ModelRuntimeOut.description:
Whether a call here would actually reach the configured service.

The default local-safe mode and `--mock` both substitute a fake client for
every kind, so a channel can read 已启用 while nothing it named was ever
contacted. Neither mode may reach a real service, and the UI must expose
that runtime fact.
ModelRuntimeOut.title: ModelRuntimeOut

post.description: The only writing route. One transaction for the whole batch.

Read, parse, diff and check — and write nothing.

There is no server-side draft to store: the candidates go to the browser and
come back as literals on confirmation. That is also why this function
contains no `session.add`, `flush` or `commit`, which a test asserts by
counting rows before and after.

One read-only listing request. Explicit, and the only thing that opens
the import gate.
